newsitem.title: USA: Family of U.S. woman killed in bombing sues Iran.
newsitem.headline: Family of U.S. woman killed in bombing sues Iran.

text.p: The family of an American student killed in a 1995 bombing of an Israeli bus sued Iran on Wednesday for allegedly sponsoring a Palestinian extremist group that claimed responsibility for the attack.

At a news conference in the U.S. Capitol, the family of Alisa Flatow, a 20-year-old New Jersey woman killed when a suicide bomber struck an Israeli bus in the Palestinian-run Gaza Strip, unveiled the suit seeking $150 million in damages.

"My family has no illusions about the road ahead of us," said Stephen Flatow, the victim's father, who called the lawsuit a first step. He vowed after his daughter's death not to seek revenge, but he said, "I would accept nothing less than justice."

The civil lawsuit named as defendants the Iranian government, its top leaders, the Iranian Ministry of Information and Security and other Iranian officials, charging that they should be held responsible for the attack.

It charged that Iran had sponsored the Palestine Islamic Jihad by providing it with about $2 million a year. A faction of the group claimed responsibility for the bus attack, according to the lawsuit.

"Alisa Flatow's death was caused by a wilful and deliberate act of ... killing because the explosion was caused by a bomb that was deliberately driven into the bus by Palestine Islamic Jihad acting under the direction and sponsorship of" Iran and the other defendants, the suit said.

It was filed under an anti-terrorism law signed by President Bill Clinton last year that allowed U.S. citizens to bring lawsuits for alleged state-sponsored terrorism. The law created an exception to the sovereign immunity that foreign governments enjoy, allowing suits for alleged terrorism.
Democratic Sen. Frank Lautenberg of New Jersey, a sponsor of the law, said Iranian officials must be held accountable for agents they pay who carry out attacks on Americans.
"Nothing can bring Alisa Flatow back to her family and friends. I do hope, however, that the award of large punitive damages in this lawsuit will spare other families the same suffering," he said.

Representative Jim Saxton, a Republican from New Jersey and another sponsor of the law, said the lawsuit represented the first of its kind in seeking punitive damages from a foreign nation for alleged state-sponsored terrorism.
Flatow, who was studying at an Israeli university, and seven Israeli soldiers were killed when a suicide bomber rammed the bus with a van loaded with explosives.

Steven Perles, lawyer for the family, said legal wrangling could take several years before the case goes to trial. He said the State Department had been cooperative so far in providing information about Iran but he had yet to have any talks with Israeli or Palestinian authorities.
